text: Pin Python deps by hash, not version: `pip install foo==1.2.3 --hash=sha256:...`. Hash mismatch fails install before code runs.
Commit your lockfile (poetry.lock / uv.lock / requirements.txt with hashes). Floating versions = future supply-chain risk.
Read every new package's setup.py / pyproject.toml before first install. 90% of supply-chain malware lives in install-time code.
For teams: run an internal PyPI mirror (Artifactory / devpi). Block direct external installs in CI.
2018 event-stream: maintainer handed off package, new owner injected wallet stealer targeting Bitpay/Copay users. 8M downloads/week before detection.
2024 xz-utils backdoor (CVE-2024-3094): 2-year social-engineering campaign to get a malicious maintainer onto xz, then sshd backdoor via liblzma. Caught by accident.
2024 ultralytics: malicious release 8.3.41/8.3.42 with XMRig crypto-miner. Pushed via compromised GitHub Actions to PyPI before maintainers noticed.
2024 lottie-player: maintainer's npm token was compromised, attacker pushed releases with obfuscated wallet drainer hitting users mid-render.
2022 ctx (PyPI): abandoned 8-year-old package taken over, new version exfiltrated AWS credentials from environment vars.
2022 colors.js / faker.js: maintainer deliberately broke own packages (`liberty` infinite loop) — not malicious supply-chain, but illustrated single-maintainer fragility.
New dependency = new attack surface. Before adding, ask: is the maintainer active? How many GitHub stars? When was the last release? Any 2FA on PyPI?
Smallest dep tree wins. is-odd, left-pad, etc. — every transitive dep is a takeover candidate. `pipdeptree` to audit yours.
Beware namespace confusion: an internal `acme-utils` package can be shadowed by a public PyPI `acme-utils`. Configure pip with `--index-url` priority.
Scope your CI tokens. A compromised PyPI publish token shouldn't be able to push to npm, GitHub, AWS. One token per service, narrow scope.
PyPI 2FA is mandatory for new accounts since 2024. Old accounts: turn it on now. Trusted Publishers (OIDC) > long-lived tokens.
`pip install --upgrade` is Russian roulette where the gun has more chambers every year.
Q: How many transitive deps does your project have? A: One too many.
Best place to hide malware: nobody reads the install-script. Second best place: the README, because nobody reads that either.
left-pad was 11 lines. The supply-chain impact was approximately the entire JavaScript ecosystem.
2024 PyTorch nightly compromise (dependency confusion): `torchtriton` was uploaded to PyPI before being claimed by Meta. Affected nightly users.
Red flags in install-script: base64 strings >400 chars, exec/eval, urlopen, subprocess('curl ...'), reads from ~/.ssh or ~/.aws. wtfguard greps for all of these.
PyPI Trusted Publishers (OIDC via GitHub Actions): no long-lived tokens, scoped per-workflow, automatic key rotation. Migrate from API tokens this quarter.
Audit your lockfile diff in every PR. `poetry lock --no-update` should produce zero diff if you didn't intend to bump anything.
Found supply-chain malware? Report to security@pypi.org (PyPI), security@npmjs.com (npm), security@rust-lang.org (cargo). They respond within hours.
